# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.

completion: When you review inspection results, you need to identify positive or presumptive test samples which must be reported. 3. A positive test for fecal bacteria is one in which the laboratory reports a fecal bacteria count greater than 10 cfu/100 mL for T/S coliforms (also described as either "fecal coliforms," "thermotolerant coliforms" or "E. coli") * Remember, this applies only to total and fecal coliform bacteria counts - Escherichia coli is not used in this formula. 4. Using only that number of positive tests that exceeds the monthly benchmark for a system of your size, construct the following formula to calculate your monthly number of MCL violations.
